title: Fruit Juice Drink with High Vitamin C

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit juice drink is a beverage obtained by pressing fresh fruits and enriched with vitamin C (5333 mg/L). It has a bright aroma, refreshing taste, and vivid colour. The juice can be made from oranges, kiwi, strawberries and other berries rich in vitamin C.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vitamin C content is ten times the daily recommended intake for an adult.
Minimal heat processing preserves most antioxidants.
Regular consumption supports immunity and speeds recovery from colds.
The drink is often used as a base for marinades, sauces and desserts.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: Vitamin C enhances the activity of immune cells, helping the body fight infections.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamin C neutralises free radicals, slowing cellular aging processes.

items.title: Improved iron absorption
items.content: Vitamin C increases the bioavailability of plant‑based iron, important for preventing anemia.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Vitamin C participates in collagen synthesis, promoting skin elasticity and repair.

items.title: Reduced fatigue
items.content: High doses of vitamin C can help lessen feelings of tiredness and boost energy levels.

items.title: Excessive vitamin C intake
items.content: Very high doses may cause gastrointestinal discomfort such as diarrhea.

items.title: Allergy to fruit components
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific fruits used in the juice.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Vitamin C can affect the efficacy of certain drugs, for example anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Consume
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, 200‑250 ml per day. It can be added to smoothies, cocktails, used as a base for fruit punches or incorporated into culinary recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the drink in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container for up to 5 days. When frozen, it can be kept for up to 3 months in portion‑size containers.
